## 1. SNAP — strongest documented starting point

[SNAP](https://snap.stanford.edu/snap-2.1/index.html) documents a C++ core intended for large networks, with dynamic nodes, edges and attributes. Those are directly relevant to graph manipulation and additional semantics.

claims.claim: Zulip documents server deployment with Docker.
claims.source_quote: Its official repository describes an open-source team-chat system under Apache 2.0 and explicitly documents running your own server on Ubuntu/Debian or with Docker.
claims.claim_context:
I would start with Zulip. It is the strongest documented fit for your mandatory requirements and your optional preference for keyboard use.

1. **Zulip — first choice.** Its official repository describes an open-source team-chat system under Apache 2.0 and explicitly documents running your own server on Ubuntu/Debian or with Docker. Its official feature matrix lists a browser interface, iOS and Android apps, and the same entirely open-source software across its plans. The keyboard reference covers navigation, searching, composing and replying, menus, and channel operations. That is strong support for your optional preference, though I have not tested whether every operation you personally need can be completed without a mouse. Its topic-organized conversation model is the main workflow difference to try before choosing it.
